notes.title: OST Update; Two Scenes To Completion
notes.notes: [h3]Devlog TLDR[/h3][list][*][p][url="https://arcanaxix.bandcamp.com/album/amadeus-a-riddle-for-thee-demo-original-soundtrack"]BandCamp album[/url] of the soundtrack has been updated with all tracks & discounted to $5[/p][/*][*][p]Track embeds with art & story snippets can be accessed [url="https://arcanaxix.com/PressKit/ost.html"]on my website here[/url][/p][/*][*][p]Game is now [b]2 scenes away[/b] from being built (with placeholders)[/p][/*][*][p]I have played through all of it and am confident in the current state[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Read on for more details. If you'd like to easily find these links later, all resources for [i]Amadeus[/i] can be accessed at [url="https://linktr.ee/amadeusgame"]linktr.ee/amadeusgame[/url]. [/p][p][/p][h3]OST Update[/h3][p]To celebrate Amadeus reaching over 700 outstanding wishlists on Steam, and also to celebrate the fact that I am almost finished building the whole thing; [b]I've updated the [url="https://arcanaxix.bandcamp.com/album/amadeus-a-riddle-for-thee-demo-original-soundtrack"]soundtrack album on BandCamp[/url][/b]. It now:[/p][list][*][p]Contains every track in the current demo; and[/p][/*][*][p]Preserves tracks from obsolete demos[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]I have also updated the embedded version on my website, which is probably the best way to experience the audio-visual atmosphere of [i]Amadeus[/i] other than playing the game. Support for high resolution screens is questionable, so you may need to zoom in if it looks off. [url="https://arcanaxix.com/PressKit/ost.html"]It can be found here[/url].[/p][p][/p][p][b][i]Thank you so much for over 700 outstanding wishlists![/i][/b][/p][p][/p][h3]Development Status[/h3][p]As with the last few before it, this past month was spent building out 3 new scenes in the game to a state of "playable." The scripts are in with some revisions, a combination of final and placeholder assets were used to flesh them out, and the scenes exist now. I spent particular attention on the music implementation and timing for these ones and I think that's feeling really effective.[/p][p][/p][p]I also took one day to play all the way through the game that I have built so far, from start-to-finish. Doing so has made me really confident about the progress I've made and the current state of the game; I'm [i]very[/i] excited to finish it and share it with the world. A lot of detail work I've done may not pay off until future episodes, but I truly believe it will make this story one worth experiencing.[/p][p][/p][h3]June Goals[/h3][p]For this coming month, my to-do list is very simple. I'm going to "finish" the game. Only two scenes and the credits remain to be built before the entirety of Episode 1 is playable, and I will knock those out this month.[/p][p][/p][p]What that means in practice is building out one last point-and-click scene, one last VN scene, and the credits. I'm looking forward to writing a devlog at the end of June that just says "GAME IS BUILT!"—from there it's about finalizing assets, polish, revisions, and playtesting.[/p][p][/p][p]For today, though, that about wraps things up. Thank you for your continued interest![/p][p][/p][p][i]For those interested, a longer version of this post can be read [url="https://arcanaxix.itch.io/amadeus-ep1-waltz/devlog/959865/ost-update-two-scenes-to-completion"]on itch.io[/url].[/i] [/p]

notes.title: January Update
notes.notes:
Last month was really good for development despite the fact that I lost a week being sick with COVID. I made good progress towards full game completion, now that I'm satisfied with the mechanics in the demo. I feel strongly oriented in the right direction.

[h3]Major accomplishments:[/h3]
[list]
[*][b] Built the next 2 point-and-click scenes[/b]
[*] Discovered & fixed a bunch of bugs [i](edge cases not present in the demo)[/i]
[*] New job with a good schedule to support work on [i]Amadeus[/i]
[*] Perhaps most importantly: [b]started reworking how I manage this project.[/b]
[/list]
Bottom line is I've figured out how to set goals for myself in a way that motivates me without getting in my own way. I am focusing proportionately more of my time directly on development, and not on micromanaging the project. This priority shift let me finish completely building two new scenes in a month where I lost [i]over a week[/i] due to illness! I'm aiming to build three more in February, and I'll let you know where we are at in next month's update.

In this same vein, please expect fewer miscellaneous social media updates for the next few months. I'm going to focus my time and energy on development rather than marketing until the game is nearly complete. [i](These monthly updates will continue, though. They keep me accountable and motivated; I enjoy looking back on what I've done each month.)[/i]

I will also still post bonus announcements for anything important that comes up. Anything I want to make sure people know about will be clearly communicated, and you can find all of the important links at [url=https://linktr.ee/amadeusgame]linktr.ee/amadeusgame[/url]! This little update is just to reassure you that silence, for the foreseeable future, is [i]a good thing.[/i] It means I am actively focusing on development.

Thank you for your continued trust and interest. Finishing this game is incredibly important to me. I will see it through.

[i]For those interested, a much longer version of this update can be read [url=https://arcanaxix.itch.io/amadeus-ep1-waltz/devlog/877961/january-devlog-setting-goals]on itch.io[/url]. If you [/i]don't[i] wish to read the long version, the most important thing mentioned in it is that the [/i]Amadeus[i] Tumblr blog now has [url=https://amadeusgame.tumblr.com/tagged/fan%20art]a dedicated fanart page[/url].[/i]

notes.title: December Update: A Year of Progress
notes.notes:
This is a brief update on the [i]Amadeus: A Riddle for Thee ~ Episode 1 ~ Waltz[/i] release timeline, and an overview on development progress made this year. If you're interested in more details, a much longer version of this update can be read [url=https://arcanaxix.itch.io/amadeus-ep1-waltz/devlog/860215/december-devlog-a-year-of-progress]on itch.io[/url].

[h3]On Episode 1's Timeline[/h3]
After launching the updated, feature-complete demo last month, I confirmed that by the end of 2024 I would have an updated timeline for the game's release. This is especially important given how many times the launch date has been pushed back this year.

I now understand why that happened and will avoid it occurring again.
[list]
[*] Episode 1's timeline was repeatedly pushed back because I realized making the game good mattered more to me than meeting an arbitrary deadline. I misjudged how much more I wanted to add to the game once I relaxed the deadline.
[*] MAGWest forced me to finish a feature-complete demo. The foundation for the game is now complete.
[*] The full episode will release in 2025.
[*] A date will not be announced until the game is nearly finished and the release is 100% certain.
[/list]
[h3]Looking Back at 2024[/h3]
A list of milestones between the original February demo release and the recent feature-complete update.
[list]
[*] February 2024 - [b]Original Demo Release[/b]
[*] March 2024 - [b]100 Wishlists on Steam[/b]
[*] April 2024  - [b]Wrote a Mystery Game[/b]
[*] June 2024 - [b]Steam Next Fest[/b] & [b]Major Narrative Benchmark[/b] (finished full episode script first draft)
[*] July 2024 - [b]Major Mechanics Benchmark[/b] (implemented most must-have mechanics)
[*] August 2024 - [b]Finished MAGWest Build[/b]
[*] September 2024 - [b]Tabled at MAGWest[/b]
[*] November 2024 - [b]Feature-Complete Demo Release[/b]
[/list]

Thank you for your interest in this game. It is in really good shape, and I'm confident the delays will have been worth it.

For more resources: [url=https://linktr.ee/amadeusgame]linktr.ee/amadeusgame[/url]

notes.title: Major Demo Update
notes.notes:
The updated demo for [i]Amadeus: A Riddle for Thee ~ Episode 1 ~ Waltz[/i] is now live. You can install and play it right now on Windows, MacOS, or Linux!

This demo includes nearly every feature intended for the final episode release, such as:

[list]
[*] Rich text that supports dramatic pauses as the text scrolls (+ "instant text" speed option)
[*] Finalized narrative that accurately introduces the full 5-episode story
[*] Save-and-Load with 3 save slots
[*] Seamless audio looping for certain tracks
[*] 2 BGM tracks with dynamic layers that respond to gameplay (+ 8 more tracks for 10 total)
[*] New cinematic opening cutscene
[*] More art, music, and a new secret mechanic
[*] Completely revamped UI design
[*] Keyboard control support in menus
[*] "Cycle through interactibles" mechanic
[*] Linux cursor disappearance issue fixed
[/list]

The only features not yet included are a "quit game" hotkey in the menu and some window options - everything else is implemented. If you've been following this game since the original demo released in February, thank you so much for your continued interest and support.

(If you've been following this game from MAGWest, this demo is very similar to the demo from that convention, but it has a whole extra scene at the end and a few additional feature requests implemented.)

From now on, development will focus exclusively on the remaining content beyond the scenes included in this demo (save for bug fixes). The full episode is coming soon - regular devlogs will continue to keep you updated in the interim, to give an idea of how soon.

This demo will likely be released as a standalone store page that can be reviewed in the coming weeks; if that happens, and you are so inclined, please leave a review. But most importantly: please enjoy the new demo. I hope it builds anticipation for the full release, which is much closer than it's ever been after reaching this major milestone.

[i]Note: the old demo is still available to play, although it is now completely obsolete and no longer accurate to the complete intended narrative. You can access it by opting into the "olddemo" beta build, which will unlock a special launch option for it. There's no reason to play this version unless you are curious about just how many new features have been added in the new build by comparison.[/i]

notes.title: Brief Update & Linux Bug Fix
notes.notes:
I'll keep this short: last month, life stuff happened, and I did not finish the overhauled demo build. It is almost ready, and it will be very worth the wait.

I also wish to announce that [b]I've addressed the bug that causes the cursor to disappear on Linux.[/b] The fix will be included in the new demo. I now have a proper Linux test machine, so no future builds should have such egregious platform-specific issues.

Not going to waste more time on words when it's better spent on development - just know the new demo build is coming very soon! Look forward to it.

notes.title: MAGWest Retrospective + Upcoming Demo Update
notes.notes:
It's been a week since Amadeus was featured at the Indie Games Expo at MAGWest, and this is intended as an update both for people who attended and found this game at the event, and people who have been following this game and are awaiting updates.

[b]For those from MAGWest:[/b] the version of the game presented at the booth isn't publicly available yet, but will be this month. The currently live demo is from February and does not include most new mechanics featured at MAGWest. More details follow.

A longer version of this log can be read on itch.io [url=https://arcanaxix.itch.io/amadeus-ep1-waltz/devlog/810763/magwest-retrospective-demo-update-this-month]here[/url].

[h3]MAGWest Recap[/h3]

The MAGWest demo build with all new mechanics was received very well. The reception at the event from people who played was overwhelmingly positive, with high praise for its music, art, sound, narrative, and atmosphere. Thank you so much for the support.

Based on feedback, the following are the most highly-requested items to be addressed in the upcoming new public demo:
[list]
[*] It's unclear that after exhausting all 3 options, selecting one again will progress the story.
[*] Collision on a particular interactible needs to be adjusted.
[*] Instead of reducing opacity on the non-active speaker in dialogue scenes, it would be less visually confusing to add a grey overlay.
[*] Keyboard controls for scrolling backlog tome need to be adjusted to account for length of backlog text.
[*] Will add an option for an "instant" text appearance speed.
[/list]
[h3]New Public Demo[/h3]

This will be the build showcased in-person at MAGWest but with a few more scenes so it roughly covers the content from the existing demo. It will be released later this month, and will likely have its own store page so it can be reviewed by those who give it a play.

That said, the full game is set to release not too long after the demo update, so whether you feel it's a must-play or not is entirely up to you. Its most important role is to accurately represent what the full episode will be like for people considering purchasing the game.

Brief overview of everything new coming in the updated demo:
[list]
[*] Rich text & more fonts
[*] Witch redesign
[*] UI indicates what you are interacting with before you click
[*] Background is highlighted along with cursor change when hovering over interactibles
[*] Speaker name is no longer part of the spoken text itself and is displayed in its own box above
[*] Text appearance can pause mid-scroll for pacing/dramatic effect
[*] Menus and settings now navigable with keyboard controls. Also fixed an issue where some text scroll settings weren't working properly across scenes
[*] Backlog redesign
[*] "Cycle through all interactibles" mechanic
[*] Glossary mechanic (to encourage big brain theorizing)
[*] Save + load from 3 save slots
[*] Opening cinematic
[*] Narrative adjustments to reflect more thorough planning
[*] Secret new mechanic :)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44894933/01b3a66d37205813c57b277b9e5bdd0924a6304e.jpg[/img]

[h3]Full Game[/h3]

The full game is coming very soon. A November release now feels overly optimistic, but by the end of 2024 seems possible. A realistic timeline will be confirmed after the demo update is published.


In lieu of a release date, here is a status update on the game's development:
[list]
[*] [b]Music [/b]- all tracks are written but a few need more TLC/development.
[*] [b]Sound[/b] - release-ready, but more sound design assets may be added as time allows.
[*] [b]Art[/b] - still need to draw a few more backgrounds and portraits.
[*] [b]Narrative[/b] - fully written, but most scenes post-demo need revision.
[*] [b]Mechanics[/b] - nearly release-ready. The small number of tweaks listed from the MAGWest build need to be implemented, but otherwise it is feeling great.
[*] [b]Build[/b] - this is what is going to take the most time, and is why a release estimate can't be given until the new demo is public.
[/list]
Thanks to MAGWest for being an important goalpost and momentum boost on the way to a full game release for Episode 1. Look forward to a big update to the public demo this month, and Episode 1 will come shortly after.

Happy werewolf season!
